lead.title: Genomes for every diploid barley relative turn Hordeum into a model for crop genome evolution
lead.summary: A consortium led from the Leibniz Institute of Plant Genetics and Crop Plant Research assembled chromosome-scale genomes for all recognised diploid Hordeum species, the wild relatives of cultivated barley, together with representative polyploid lineages. The comparison reveals extensive inversions and chromosomal rearrangements that break collinearity near the centromeres, pervasive ancient hybridisation and introgression, and widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses, with many of the transferred genes transcribed and apparently functionally integrated. Coding sequences stay highly conserved across the genus while regulatory elements turn over rapidly, and case studies on vernalization and glume development show how that regulatory variation feeds into flowering time and floral morphology. For breeders the practical payoff is a map of where useful wild variation sits and how structural variation will constrain moving it into barley.

notes.label: Plant science
notes.text: Timing and signalling dominated: cool nights flatten a morning peak of OsRLCK309 and leave rice open to blast, photo-activated phytochrome A destabilises COP1 through DET1 under far-red light, and lanosterol turns out to be the precursor of the solanoeclepins that potato roots secrete to hatch cyst nematodes.

notes.label: Biotech
notes.text: Tool-building was the theme: OsPLT7 drives synthetic apomixis in rice without a fertility cost, EPFL9 editing steps down stomatal density in an elite poplar, a mild sugarcane mosaic virus isolate becomes an agroinoculated overexpression vector for maize and sorghum, and a transgene-free 10 bp insertion in OsC1 makes haploid seedlings visible by eye.

notes.label: Prairies
notes.text: Prairie-relevant threads: an Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada study of recurrent selection for freezing tolerance in alfalfa and what it does to root and nodule microbiomes, CRISPR knockout of BnPHT5;1a in Brassica napus to cut arsenic uptake, and a 374-isolate European survey of multidrug resistance in Zymoseptoria tritici. The alfalfa work is the only Canadian study here, and it was an unheated greenhouse experiment rather than a field trial.

plant.title: A chromosome-scale genome for every diploid Hordeum species reopens the barley gene pool
plant.summary: The team assembled all recognised diploid Hordeum species plus representative polyploids and found extensive inversions and rearrangements, ancient hybridisation and segmental exchange, and widespread horizontal gene transfer from Panicoideae grasses into Hordeum. Retrotransposon proliferation explains most genome size variation. Coding sequence is conserved while regulatory elements turn over fast, which the authors illustrate with vernalization and glume development.

plant.title: Cool nights blunt a morning immune peak and leave rice open to blast
plant.summary: Cool-night pre-exposure weakened rice blast resistance and lowered morning expression of a set of receptor-like cytoplasmic kinase genes. OsRLCK309 is a positive regulator of pattern-triggered immunity that associates with the chitin co-receptor OsCERK1 and is phosphorylated at Ser245 and Thr246; OsCCA1 gives it a morning peak under warm nights, while cool nights flatten that peak and induce OsDREB1A, which shifts expression into the night. Mutating the two OsDREB1A binding sites in the promoter preserved resistance after cool nights, with minimal agronomic trade-offs under the conditions tested.

plant.title: Lanosterol is the precursor of the root signals that hatch potato cyst nematodes
plant.summary: Solanoeclepins are heavily modified triterpenoids secreted by tomato and potato roots that act as potent hatching factors for potato cyst nematodes, and their origin was unknown. Tomato hairy roots lacking lanosterol synthase made no lanosterol and far less solanoeclepin; exogenous lanosterol restored production, and deuterium-labelled lanosterol was incorporated directly. The work is in hairy roots rather than whole plants, but it gives the entry point for engineering or blocking the hatching cue.

plant.title: A rice peptide intercepts a planthopper salivary protein and raises grain weight at the same time
plant.summary: Screening eight planthopper-specific salivary proteins found that SP4 binds OsWIH2, a cysteine-rich rice peptide strongly induced by brown planthopper infestation. Overexpressing OsWIH2 cut feeding, honeydew excretion, nymph survival and fecundity of Nilaparvata lugens in both pot and field trials, through salicylic acid signalling rather than jasmonate. The overexpression lines also grew better with larger, heavier grain, which is an unusual escape from the usual defence and yield trade-off, though the result rests on transgenic overexpression rather than natural alleles.

plant.title: Metabolomes of 312 pear accessions trace flavour domestication in two steps
plant.summary: Integrating metabolomes, variomes and proteomes across 312 diverse pear accessions, the authors show metabolic diversity shrank during domestication and improvement. Early domestication cut bitterness, astringency and gritty stone cell content to make the fruit edible, while later breeding selected sugars and organic acids for flavour. They identify CCCH15 as a new regulator of stone cell formation, describe an antagonism between malic and citric acid tied to linked genetic variation, and link MYB114 promoter haplotypes to red flesh.

plant.title: A Ryd4 barley hybrid blocks barley yellow dwarf virus at several points along the aphid route
plant.summary: University of Nottingham researchers dissected resistance in the barley hybrid SY Kestrel, which carries a Hordeum bulbosum-derived Ryd4 introgression, to barley yellow dwarf virus and its vector Rhopalosiphum padi. They found constitutive volatile-mediated deterrence before settling, impaired phloem feeding and reduced aphid fitness afterwards, and suppressed virus establishment, alongside maintained photosystem II function and reprogrammed oxylipin metabolism. Usefully for breeders, the study separates core Ryd4 effects from extra defences carried by the larger introgressed background.

plant.title: A bacterial wilt effector jams assembly of the jasmonate receptor
plant.summary: Jasmonate signalling turns out to help plants resist the hemibiotroph Ralstonia solanacearum, and the bacterium answers with the effector RipBO. RipBO binds the F-box domain of the receptor COI1 with high affinity, competitively displaces the COI1 and ASK interaction, and so blocks assembly of the SCF complex, stabilising JAZ repressors and paralysing jasmonate immunity. The mechanism is worked out in Arabidopsis, so the relevance to wilt in solanaceous crops still has to be shown.

plant.title: Phytochrome A destabilises COP1 under far-red light, inverting the usual photoreceptor relationship
plant.summary: COP1 is the central repressor of photomorphogenesis and normally degrades photoreceptors, including phytochrome A. Here the authors show the traffic runs both ways: while phytochrome B and the cryptochromes promote COP1 accumulation under red and blue light, photo-activated phytochrome A drives COP1 degradation through the 26S proteasome under far-red-rich light such as canopy shade, in a process dependent on DET1. COP1 itself helps assemble the phyA, COP1 and DET1 complex. The work is Arabidopsis-only, but the authors frame it as relevant to acclimation under high planting density.

plant.title: A KNOX and BELL module builds lignin to keep rice leaves flat and drought tolerant
plant.summary: RLC3, also called OsBLH4, is a BELL-type homeodomain transcription factor identified through two mutant alleles and CRISPR knockouts. Losing it shrinks bulliform cells, disrupts lignin biosynthesis and secondary cell wall formation, and leaves the midrib vasculature malformed, which speeds water loss and rolls the leaf. RLC3 activates core lignin genes including OsCCR4, OsCAld5H1, OsPAL5 and OsCOMT5, and heterodimerises with the KNOX factors OSH1, OSH45 and OSH71 to co-activate subsets of them.

plant.title: Growth and reproduction trade off in woody plants, but the trade-off is weakening
plant.summary: A synthesis of 685 estimates from 78 studies covering 79 woody species, concentrated at northern temperate latitudes, found growth and seed production negatively correlated within the same year, consistent with an immediate cost of reproduction. The correlations were not systematically related to functional traits or climate, and were strongest in species with highly variable interannual seed production. In those species the trade-off has weakened markedly over recent decades, which the authors read as a sign that shifting reproductive variability is changing how trees allocate resources.

biotech.title: OsPLT7 drives synthetic apomixis in rice without the usual fertility cost
biotech.summary: Synthetic apomixis would let hybrid rice seed reproduce clonally and fix heterosis, but existing routes depend on BABY BOOM genes and tend to come with poor seed set. This report identifies OsPLT7, a PLETHORA family factor that is not a BBM gene, as an alternative trigger for clonal seed formation that the authors say does not compromise fertility. PubMed carries no abstract for the paper, so the induction and fertility figures could not be checked from the record.

biotech.title: Editing EPFL9 steps stomatal density down in an elite poplar cultivar
biotech.summary: Working from the first complete genome of the elite poplar cultivar Beilinxiongzhu 1, the authors edited the stomatal development gene EPFL9 and recovered a graded series of lower stomatal densities rather than a single knockout phenotype. The lines lost less water and used water more efficiently under drought. This is a nursery-scale result in a tree, so it says nothing yet about rotation-length growth or wood properties.

biotech.title: A DELLA-evading transcription factor isoform lifts wheat grain weight without undoing semi-dwarfing
biotech.summary: The Rht-B1b and Rht-D1b alleles behind Green Revolution semi-dwarf wheat encode DELLA proteins that also hold back grain development. The authors show Rht-B1b works partly by suppressing a specific isoform of the transcription factor DL, DL-B.4, and that NEK6-mediated phosphorylation of DL-B.4 cancels that suppression, raising GA20ox3 expression and gibberellin intermediates in the grain. Overexpression and natural DL-B.4 variants raised grain weight without changing plant height.

biotech.title: First field trial of GM barley carrying the wheat aluminium tolerance gene TaALMT1
biotech.summary: Embrapa researchers introgressed TaALMT1, the major aluminium resistance gene of hexaploid wheat, into four barley cultivars adapted to southern Brazil and tested homozygous lines against null segregants for two years on an acid soil and a nearby limed area. In the first year, with very high aluminium and below-average rainfall, the better GM lines yielded 5.9 to 72.8 times more grain than their controls, which the authors translate to a potential 0.7 to 1.7 t per hectare. In the wetter second year, with lower aluminium, there was no measurable yield advantage, so the benefit looks tied to dry seasons and deeper rooting.

biotech.title: A multi-omics prediction platform picks a hybrid rice line that outyielded its checks in field tests
biotech.summary: DNNGP-Pro combines convolutional networks for local omics features, graph convolution over a shared-parent graph of hybrids, and a transformer for long-range dependencies. Adding the shared-parent graph lifted accuracy by 2.98 to 5.54 per cent for single-omics data across 13 traits in four populations, and dual-omics models ran 5.33 to 9.23 per cent above single-omics. Trained on 1,040 hybrids from a 26,040-hybrid population, it picked the indica hybrid Chunliangyou825, which yielded 23.62 and 8.01 per cent above two checks at Hangzhou and 7.70 and 16.15 per cent above them at Pingxiang, and has been submitted for variety certification.

biotech.title: A mild sugarcane mosaic virus isolate becomes a transient expression vector for maize and sorghum
biotech.summary: Stable transformation in maize and sorghum is slow and costly, and existing viral vectors cause severe symptoms or need awkward inoculation. The authors found a mild sugarcane mosaic virus isolate, SCmDu, and built it into an agroinoculated overexpression vector; co-expressing the silencing suppressor TP22 and maize ZmEIF4A3 in Nicotiana benthamiana gave titres high enough for simple mechanical transmission to maize seedlings. Expression held systemically for over four weeks across diverse inbreds, tolerated large fusions, worked in sorghum, and was used to identify ZmGA2ox6 as a plant height regulator.

biotech.title: A purple coleoptile marker makes rice haploids visible to the eye
biotech.summary: Doubled haploid breeding in rice has advanced with inducers such as HI285, but telling haploids apart remains the bottleneck, and sorting by seedling size gives many false positives while discarding spontaneous doubled haploids. The authors engineered the anthocyanin gene OsC1 into HI285, either by overexpression or by a precise 10 bp insertion, giving a coleoptile purple line marker that allows instant scoring at the seedling stage without losing induction efficiency. The insertion line, HI285-Red, is transgene-free.

biotech.title: A step-by-step route to complete CRISPR knockouts in tetraploid potato
biotech.summary: Knocking out all alleles in cultivated potato is hard because the crop is vegetatively propagated and highly heterozygous tetraploid. Working in cultivar Desiree, the authors show repeated de novo regeneration raises editing efficiency by letting new mutations appear, and set out detection strategies for targets without an obvious phenotype in polyploid and possibly mosaic material. Their case study knocked out StBEL5, a tuberisation regulator, and found only slightly delayed tuber onset and comparable yields, suggesting the gene matters less in tuberosum than in andigena.

biotech.title: Editing a vacuolar phosphate transporter cuts arsenic uptake in oilseed rape
biotech.summary: Simultaneous CRISPR/Cas9 editing of both Brassica napus homeologs of the vacuolar phosphate influx transporter BnPHT5;1a gave double mutants with better arsenate tolerance. Under 400 micromolar arsenate their shoot and root fresh weights were 11.0 to 30.1 per cent higher and root arsenic about 28 per cent lower than wild type, and disruption lowered expression of several plasma membrane PHT1 genes, an effect that faded as external phosphate fell. Yeast assays gave no evidence the protein transports arsenate itself, so the authors read the result as avoidance rather than transport, and the work is hydroponic rather than field based.

biotech.title: A tetraploid wild barley genome adds saline-alkali tolerance to the Hordeum toolkit
biotech.summary: Tetraploid Hordeum brevisubulatum is a strongly saline-alkali tolerant wild relative of barley that had no reference genome. The authors produced a chromosome-scale assembly, resolved its A and B subgenomes, and found distinct evolutionary histories, homeolog-specific expression under stress, and structural variants overlapping gene bodies and regulatory regions. The transcription factor HbNAC29 was strongly induced in leaf and root, its homeologs differ structurally in their regulatory regions, and heterologous overexpression in rice supported a role in tolerance.

ag.title: Tropical land-use intensification reorganises biodiversity rather than simply homogenising it
ag.summary: An ecosystem-wide assessment of 24 taxonomic groups covering 40,049 species, along a gradient from Indonesian lowland forest to intensively managed smallholder cash-crop monoculture, found landscape multidiversity down about 78 per cent and local multidiversity about 50 per cent in monocultures. Despite those losses there was no consistent community homogenisation; aboveground taxa shifted systematically from turnover to nestedness. The authors argue this differentiation can partly buffer gamma diversity, which leaves room for management through remnants of traditional agriculture, while cautioning that it may mask an early stage on the way to homogenisation.

ag.title: Multidrug resistance in Zymoseptoria tritici is quantitative and runs past the MFS1 promoter
ag.summary: Across 374 field isolates collected in Europe in 2020 and 2021, the authors catalogued MFS1 promoter polymorphism and found six new structural variants derived from different transposable elements, confirming repeated independent insertion. Previously characterised inserts consistently confer resistance, but several new variants have limited or variable effect, and crosses plus quantitative phenotyping and a genome-wide association study showed multidrug resistance behaves as a quantitative trait with additional candidate genes in detoxification and membrane transport. The authors conclude single-locus genotyping is not enough for monitoring, and that current resistance management may be selecting for broad-spectrum resistance.

ag.title: Six years of grape trials put a defence-inducing biofungicide in rotations, not in place of fungicides
ag.summary: From 2017 to 2022 near Geneva, New York, researchers tested Bacillus mycoides isolate J alone and in rotation with conventional fungicides against grapevine downy and powdery mildew in randomised complete block trials. Programme by year interactions were significant for all eight disease, tissue and endpoint combinations. Isolate J alone usually beat untreated controls but lagged conventional programmes in several 2017 to 2019 comparisons, while rotations containing it were often indistinguishable from conventional programmes, so the authors position it as an integrated management component rather than a substitute.

ag.title: Brazilian sunflower looper populations stay broadly susceptible, with methomyl the warning sign
ag.summary: After Rachiplusia nu evolved resistance to Cry1Ac soybean, control has leaned on insecticides, so the authors paired phenotypic monitoring of 17 insecticides across nine IRAC mode-of-action groups with F2 screens for five of them. Mortality generally exceeded 94 per cent, but susceptibility fell most for triflumuron, methoxyfenozide, methomyl and metaflumizone from the 2023/24 season on. F2 screens detected resistance alleles only for methomyl and lambda-cyhalothrin, at estimated frequencies of 0.0992 and 0.0557, which the authors read as incipient resistance.

ag.title: Crabgrass resistance to nicosulfuron comes from detoxification, not a changed target
ag.summary: A resistant Digitaria sanguinalis biotype from maize fields showed no amino acid substitutions at the known acetolactate synthase resistance positions, and no difference in ALS expression or enzyme sensitivity, but higher glutathione S-transferase activity and faster loss of parent herbicide. Pretreatment with the cytochrome P450 inhibitor malathion or the GST inhibitor NBD-Cl restored sensitivity. Transcriptomics pointed to DsCYP78A9 and DsGSTU10, and expressing either in yeast improved growth under nicosulfuron, rimsulfuron and tembotrione, which implies cross-resistance risk across chemistries.

ag.source: Journal of Agricultural and Food Chemistry
ag.title: Alternative splicing of a succinate dehydrogenase subunit shapes intrinsic SDHI resistance in Fusarium graminearum
ag.summary: The authors found alternative splicing of FgSdhC1 in both SDHI-sensitive and intrinsically resistant Fusarium graminearum isolates, producing four isoforms in each background, and swapped them into isogenic strains. Individual isoforms shifted sensitivity to pydiflumetofen, boscalid and fluopyram differently and changed fitness traits, with a mean compound fitness index of 0.54 for isoforms from the resistant background against 0.20 from the sensitive one, and a high of 1.43. The work implies splicing variation, not just target-site mutation, affects how head blight responds to SDHI fungicides.

ag.title: Breeding alfalfa for freezing tolerance also shifts its root and nodule microbiomes
ag.summary: Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada researchers compared recurrently selected and unselected populations of two alfalfa cultivars across three seasonal transitions, from non-acclimated growth through cold acclimation to spring regrowth. The more freezing-tolerant populations had greater root biomass in spring and distinct metabolite profiles, and those shifts went with changes in root and nodule microbial community structure, strongest for nodule bacteria during regrowth. Season rather than selection level drove nifH copy number and estimated endophytic Sinorhizobium meliloti populations. The experiment was run in an unheated greenhouse, not in the field.

ag.source: Journal of the Royal Society Interface
ag.title: A behaviour and epidemiology model says UK integrated pest management uptake will fall far short of target
ag.summary: Coupling an epidemiological model of Septoria tritici blotch in wheat to a model of grower decision making, the authors projected only 2.16 per cent adoption of integrated pest management by 2030, missing the reduction target in the UK Pesticides National Action Plan 2025. Policies aimed at behavioural barriers, mainly knowledge and access to training and services, moved adoption most, ahead of research investment or financial subsidy, and an initial push for early adoption improved the odds of hitting time-bound targets. These are model projections under stated assumptions, not observed adoption.

ag.title: A natural volatile sulfide suppresses banana Fusarium wilt in greenhouse soil
ag.summary: Dimethyl trisulfide inhibited 11 fungal pathogens from seven hosts in vitro with half-maximal effective concentrations spanning 0.34 to 100.37 microlitres per litre, a very wide pathogen-specific range. Soil fumigation at a non-phytotoxic 80 microlitres per litre cut the Fusarium oxysporum f. sp. cubense wilt index by 94.26 per cent and vascular discoloration by 80.81 per cent against untreated controls. The trials were greenhouse only, and the authors stress dose has to be matched to the target pathogen.

ag.title: Genomic selection predicts sugarcane borer resistance well enough to skip some field screening
ag.summary: Using historical infestation data for 112 commercial and elite Louisiana sugarcane clones evaluated across 15 environments, the authors compared genomic selection models under five-fold cross-validation. Bayesian models performed best, and adding three markers identified by association mapping and stepwise regression as fixed effects raised prediction accuracy to 0.67. Coincidence indices of 0.74 for the top quarter and 0.75 for the bottom quarter of clones suggest the models can flag the most and least resistant material early, saving labour-intensive field trials.

methods: Coverage window: 17 to 20 November 2026 (about 72 hours). The previous issue was 2026-11-17, so the 18 and 19 November issues are missing and the window was widened to the last issue to avoid a gap; nothing from 15 to 17 November was repeated. Items were found through PubMed searches filtered on entry date across plant science, biotechnology, genomics, pathology, entomology and pest management journals, and every date in this issue comes from the PubMed record. Publisher and news sites were again not reachable from this session: www.wbur.org failed to resolve and would need to be allowed in the session's network settings, so three news threads surfaced by web search are mentioned here rather than listed as items because their dates and details could not be confirmed against a primary source. Those were a Penn State disease-resistant cacao line reported on 19 November 2026, a BASF announcement on 16 November 2026 of a Nemasphere nematode-resistance trait for soybean said to be available in the United States and Brazil from 2028, which is a company claim, and earlier November reports of UK Defra clearance for two Phytoform gene-edited tomato traits and a Bayer licence of nitrogen-fixation editing technology from the University of California, Davis. Today's briefing is therefore journal-only. Arabidopsis-only results are flagged: the phytochrome A and COP1 study and the RipBO effector work on jasmonate immunity. Also flagged are greenhouse and controlled-environment results without field data (the alfalfa freezing tolerance microbiome study, the dimethyl trisulfide banana trials, the BnPHT5;1a hydroponics), hairy-root rather than whole-plant work (solanoeclepin biosynthesis), transgenic overexpression rather than natural alleles (OsWIH2), and modelled projections rather than observed behaviour (the integrated pest management adoption study). The OsPLT7 apomixis paper has no abstract in PubMed, which is stated in its summary. Three Hordeum items appear across sections because the genus had an unusually busy window; they are separate studies from separate groups. No preprints are included, and no company claim is listed as an item.
